answers.note: If this is for the admin portal only, I think I'd like to add some actual color to our charts for better visibility. Would love the admin portal to feel like an F1 dashboard. A bit minimalist, cool motion graphics/animations, high information density without feeling crowded, etc. The F1 UI from Apple's recent F1 movie is specifically what I'm referencing if you could find inspo visuals, else I could probably hunt some down. Don't want to imply I want a generic F1 feel.
Dark mode will also receive the previously mentioned new colors to enhance charts, graphs, and information conveyance.

This section could use a lot of design polish; looks bad crunched tightly 2col (would benefit going wider on desktop), too much explanatory text (nobody reads all that), all 3 visuals are rough. Not sure if this was meant to reflect production version or just settle pace. This feels a bit more calm than the 2.5s, but still fast enough to likely catch attention from a scrolling visitor. That's a good general policy on our animations - shouldn't feel overwhelming, a bit more fluid/calm but with enough looped motion that they never sit still long enough for a scrolling visitor to miss a step of the motion, that way they get interested and pause to continue watching. Again, punchy copy and cool visuals always win over dense word blocks.
We'll end up switching this anyway pre-launch, with a brand new media kit, mostly generated in Higgsfield.

While this isn't perfect and could use a better design touch, it'd be a really neat easter egg delight if we included a subtle hint these images were clickable, with a fun little lightbox preview when clicked. However, it should clearly feel like a fun easter egg demo, not trap visitors in a demo they didn't ask for. This may fall on its face completely on next review, in which case we'll likely just make the images not clickable in this animation for simplicity. To be honest, a lot of the marketing visuals we've created will likely be completely replaced or revamped - most marketing pages are in very early shapes right now and feel nowhere close to complete yet, especially while we're still reshaping the app features a bit. I have a separate note I can send later about prioritizing app work near-term to fully unlock the end visions for marketing and admin, otherwise we're having to constantly reshape those off of trickle-down app changes rather than work towards polish.
